title: From Diana's Tree
text:
she says she knows nothing of the fear of the death of love

she says she is afraid of the death of love

she says that love is death is fear

she says that death is fear is love

she says she does not know


only thirst

silence

no encounter


beware of me my love

beware of the silent woman in the desert

of the traveler with the empty glass

and of the shadow of her shadow
editorial_note: The translation keeps the incantatory she says and the poem's bare, unpunctuated warnings.

title: Ashes
text:
The night splintered into stars

looking at me hallucinated

the air throws hatred

its face beautified

with music.


Soon we shall leave


Arcane dream

ancestor of my smile

the world is gaunt

and there is a padlock but no keys

and there is terror but no tears.


What shall I do with myself?


Because to You I owe what I am


But I have no tomorrow


Because to You I...


The night suffers.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the broken invocation to You and the abrupt ellipsis before the final line.

title: Salvation
text:
The island escapes.

And the girl climbs the wind again

and discovers the death of the prophet bird.

Now

it is the subdued fire.

Now

it is the flesh

..the leaf

..the stone

lost in the fountain of torment

like the navigator in the horror of civilization

that purifies the fall of night.

Now

the girl finds the mask of infinity

and breaks the wall of poetry.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated Now and the double-dot line markings from the source.

title: The Sun Like a Great Animal Too Yellow...
text:
The sun like a great animal too yellow. It is lucky that no one

helps me. Nothing is more dangerous, when one needs help, than receiving help.


But no sun kills my night.


Will I have time to make myself a mask when I emerge from shadow?


I test myself in the language in which I verify the weight of my dead.


The sea hides its dead. Because what is below must remain below.
editorial_note: The prose-poem structure is kept taut, including the clipped logic around help and concealment.

title: Rings of Ash
text:
They are my voices singing

so that they will not sing,

the grayly gagged ones at dawn,

those dressed as desolate birds in the rain.


There is, in the waiting,

a rumor of lilac breaking.

And there is, when day comes,

a division of sun into little black suns.

And when it is night, always,

a tribe of mutilated words

seeks asylum in my throat

so that they will not sing,

the disastrous ones, the owners of silence.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the paradox of voices singing so they will not sing.

title: Someday from One Side of the Moon...
text:
Someday from one side of the moon

you will see fall the kisses that shine in me

the shadows will smile haughtily

displaying the secret that moans wandering

the impassive leaves will come

that one day were

what my eyes were

the withered fragrances will come

that innate descended from the winged sound

the red joys will come

that bubble intensely

in the sun that rounds the equidistant harmonies

in the dancing smoke

of the pipe of my love.
editorial_note: The translation leaves the early surreal syntax strange rather than smoothing its leaps.

title: Days Against Reverie
text:
Not wanting whites rolling

on a movable sole.

Not wanting voices stealing

seedy arched aerial ones.

Not wanting to live a thousand oxygens,

trifles crossed toward the sky.

Not wanting to move my curve

without waxing the present leaf.

Not wanting to defeat the magnet,

the espadrille unravels.

Not wanting to touch abstracts,

to reach my last brown hair.

Not wanting to defeat soft tails,

the trees place the leaves.

Not wanting to bring, without chaos,

portable words.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's opacity and uses sole to echo the later espadrille image.

title: The Cage
text:
Outside there is sun.

It is nothing but a sun

But men look at it

and then they sing.

I know nothing of the sun.

I know the angel's melody

and the hot sermon

of the last wind.

I know how to scream until dawn

when death settles naked

on my shadow.

I weep beneath my name.

I wave handkerchiefs in the night

and thirsty for reality

they dance with me

I hide nails

to mock my sick dreams.

Outside there is sun.

I dress myself in ashes.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the contrast between the outside sun and the speaker's ash-clad interior.

title: Outside There Is Sun...
text:

editorial_note: This version mirrors the related poem while preserving it as a separate translated source text.

title: I Hear the Water Falling in My Dream Resound...
text:
I hear the water falling in my dream resound.

Words fall like water I fall. I draw

in my eyes the shape of my eyes, I swim in my

waters, I tell myself my silences. All night

I wait for my language to manage to configure me. And

I think of the wind that comes to me, remains

in me. All night I have walked under the unknown

rain. I have been given a silence

full of forms and visions (you say). And you run desolate

like the only bird in the wind.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the prose enjambments and the self-reflexive shaping by language.
